purpose: Re-run docs/handoffs/evidence/T30's build and trigger in a baseline-clean window, and check the result against T30/build.json field by field.
why_additive: T30/build.json is the historic record of the first build and is bound by docs/handoffs/evidence/T30/SHA256SUMS. Editing it would change bytes an existing record cites. This file is a second-window conformance measurement laid alongside it, not a correction of it.

reachability.problem: docs/handoffs/evidence/T30/ is not present in this branch's tree. This branch was cut from origin/integration/live-bridge-2026-11-03 at bcb7a30, and the T30 evidence landed later on member-3/t62-host-safe at c274893, which is not an ancestor of this branch's HEAD.
reachability.where_it_is: commit c274893 on member-3/t62-host-safe (and origin/member-3/t62-host-safe); 11 files, 936 insertions
reachability.how_to_verify_without_checking_out: git cat-file -p c274893:docs/handoffs/evidence/T30/build/original.elf | sha256sum  ->  c9c2632e...23c9; git cat-file -s ... -> 25344
reachability.checked: done on 2026-11-05 on this host; the blob in that commit is the same 25,344 bytes and the same digest the guest printed in 02-build.txt
reachability.consequence: every T30/... path in this record is a reference to that commit, not to a sibling directory. A reviewer reading only this branch cannot resolve them by path.

include_main.question: why does this link when the retired synthetic src.c did not
include_main.answer: original.c guards its main with #ifdef INCLUDEMAIN at line 91 and the gcc command does not define INCLUDEMAIN, so the case file contributes no main; harness.c is the only one. The synthetic src.c in fixtures/public/CWE416_Use_After_Free__malloc_free_char_01 had an unguarded main at line 90, which is why record 116 saw 'multiple definition of main'.
measured: build.sh gcc line: no -DINCLUDEMAIN (contrast: the CWE122 recipe passes -DINCLUDEMAIN -DOMITGOOD deliberately, because there the case main is the intended entry point)
harness.c line 21: extern declaration of ..._bad, line 23: int main(void)
include_main.conclusion: Record 116's link failure was a fixture-authoring defect in the synthetic src.c, not a toolchain or window problem. The upstream case and the T30 recipe are internally consistent.

output.note: byte-identical to docs/handoffs/evidence/T30/build/original.elf at commit c274893. No second artefact was created, so there is no new hash to fork.
